questions.question: What does HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language, the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.

questions.question: Which doctype declaration is correct for modern HTML5 documents?
questions.explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> is the standard, case-insensitive doctype declaration for HTML5.

questions.question: Which element is used to define metadata such as character encoding and viewport settings?
questions.explanation: The <meta> tag inside the <head> section specifies metadata like charset, viewport settings, page description, and keywords.

questions.question: Which HTML5 semantic element is best suited for self-contained content like a blog post or news article?
questions.explanation: The <article> element represents a self-contained composition in a document, page, or site, which is independently distributable or reusable.

questions.question: What is the key difference between <strong> and <b> elements?
questions.a: <strong> represents strong importance/urgency, while <b> draws attention without extra importance
questions.d: There is no difference in semantics or rendering
questions.explanation: <strong> gives semantic emphasis and strong importance (read with emphasis by screen readers), whereas <b> is purely stylistic to draw attention.

questions.question: Which attribute on an <input> element ensures that the form cannot be submitted if the field is empty?
questions.explanation: The boolean attribute 'required' specifies that an input field must be filled out before submitting the form.

questions.question: How do you associate a <label> element explicitly with an <input> element?
questions.a: By matching label's 'for' attribute with input's 'name' attribute
questions.b: By matching label's 'for' attribute with input's 'id' attribute
questions.c: By setting label's 'to' attribute to input's 'id'
questions.d: By placing them in the same <div>
questions.explanation: The 'for' attribute of <label> must match the 'id' attribute of the corresponding form element to establish programmatic association.

questions.question: Which input type provides a user-friendly slider control?
questions.explanation: <input type="range"> renders a slider control allowing selection of a numeric value within a range.

questions.question: Which attribute on an tag is essential for providing alternative text for screen readers and SEO?
questions.explanation: The 'alt' attribute provides alternative text when images cannot be displayed and is read by screen readers for accessibility.

questions.question: What is the recommended element pairing for displaying an image with an associated caption?
questions.explanation: <figure> encloses the media item and <figcaption> provides the caption or legend.

questions.question: What does the ARIA acronym stand for in web accessibility?
questions.explanation: ARIA stands for Accessible Rich Internet Applications, a set of attributes that define ways to make web content and applications more accessible.

questions.question: Which element should only be used ONCE per page to represent the main heading of the content for optimal SEO and accessibility?
questions.explanation: Having a single <h1> heading per page that describes the main topic is a fundamental SEO and screen-reader accessibility best practice.

questions.question: Which attribute should be added to external links with target="_blank" for security preventing tab-napping?
questions.explanation: rel="noopener noreferrer" prevents the newly opened page from accessing window.opener, mitigating security risks like reverse tabnapping.

questions.question: Which HTML element represents the main content area of the <body>, excluding headers, footers, and sidebars?
questions.explanation: The <main> tag represents the dominant content of the <body> of a document.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the <picture> element in HTML5?
questions.b: To provide multiple image sources for responsive art direction and resolution switching
questions.c: To capture photo input from a user device camera
questions.d: To apply CSS filter effects to embedded images
questions.explanation: The element wraps multiple elements and one to support responsive images and modern formats (like AVIF/WebP).
